publication_review.what_that_settles: There is no licence election to make, no corresponding-source obligation, and no 'derived' or 'verbatim' code in this tree. Citations stay: they are the provenance of the hardware and protocol facts and how a reader verifies them. Recorded in docs/PROVENANCE_INVENTORY.md and docs/PUBLICATION_REVIEW.md.

The push is of the committed tree verified from a clean clone; untracked in-progress sources are not part of it.

ruling.statement: It was confirmed on 2026-09-10 that no third-party code was used; the references were read for how the hardware behaves.
ruling.effect: Every file/source pair formerly classified 'derived' or 'verbatim' is 'consulted': the hardware or protocol behaviour was learned by reading and then implemented independently. No licence election is made or owed, no corresponding source is owed, and every citation is retained.
ruling.retained_license_texts: The permissive texts under licenses/ stay as acknowledgments of references consulted, not as notices for incorporated code. The Cypress CYW43455 firmware EULA is the exception: those binaries are redistributed as they are and are covered by their own terms.

classifications.original: written for Anvil; no third-party material.
classifications.hardware-facts: register offsets, bit positions, magic values, timings and required orderings taken from a datasheet, manual, device tree or a vendor header of definitions. Facts, not expression.
classifications.protocol-facts: wire formats and constants taken from a published protocol specification (RFC, IEEE, USB-IF).
classifications.interface-facts: command names, argument grammar and documented defaults modelled on a third-party console so transcripts transfer. The implementation is original.
classifications.consulted: hardware or protocol behaviour learned by reading a third-party implementation or document and then implemented independently. The citation records where the fact can be checked; no code was taken.
classifications.reference-only: cited as corroboration or as a candidate basis; no material taken.

relocations.note: COMPLETED 2026-09-10 by the driver-module lane. The AVS temperature register half of thermal.pi4 - the bcm2711.dtsi node and its three soc ranges, the AVS_RO_TEMP_STATUS offset and validity mask, and the two device-tree coefficients - now lives in a separately compiled module, whole and with its citations, and thermal.pi4 says where it went. The two rows moved with it, and two more were added: RaspberryPi4/Board/hw_mod.pi4 carries the same device-tree address translation in its device table, and RaspberryPi4/Tests/module_pipeline_emitted_gate.pi4 restates the conversion so the gate can check its direction. All three are untracked work in progress, and this check refuses to classify a file it cannot see in the index, so their rows are NOT here yet. Classify RaspberryPi4/Modules/thermal_avs.pi4 and RaspberryPi4/Board/hw_mod.pi4 against linux-dt-bcm2711 and linux-v6.12 (hw_mod.pi4 also vendor-spec), and RaspberryPi4/Tests/module_pipeline_emitted_gate.pi4 against linux-dt-bcm2711, in the same commit that tracks them - in PROVENANCE.json AND in docs/PROVENANCE_INVENTORY.md, because this check compares the two. No attribution was removed, restated or weakened: every citation that existed still exists, in the file that now holds the fact.
